format: OSwind primary-source competitor check and expansion queue
scope: Documentation rechecks plus four additional profiles now integrated into the canonical20-offering comparison. No competitor app installation, purchase, agreement, code reuse or runtime/power measurement is established by these notes.

existingChecks.name: Screenpipe
existingChecks.observation: Annual pricing still displays Basic $250 and Business $500/seat. Free history is limited. The source license distinguishes official builds from commercial source builds and restricts competing-product use without a commercial license. No code copied or runtime tested.

existingChecks.name: Original Rewind / Limitless
existingChecks.observation: Homepage timed out twice. The September 9, 2026 help article describes account exports containing transcripts, chats and optional audio, with smaller date-range exports suggested for large histories. Current homepage/service/pricing was not reverified.

existingChecks.name: Rewind Desktop (rewind.app)
existingChecks.observation: Homepage still describes local screen history and optional encrypted user-owned S3 archive with on-demand older video. The comparison URL returned a cache miss; the prior $30/month comparison claim was not freshly confirmed.

existingChecks.name: Pieces
existingChecks.observation: Monthly Pro $18.99/user and Enterprise $22.99/user, 7-day card-required trial, no free plan stated. On-device memory, recaps and MCP are advertised; Enterprise adds organization policy and provider/API-key controls.

existingChecks.name: Littlebird
existingChecks.observation: Basic is free; displayed annual Plus is $204 ($17/month equivalent), Power $510 ($42.50/month equivalent); Pro starts at $100/month. Team starts at $17/seat/month annual, Enterprise custom. Privacy page says data is stored on US-East AWS and selected context goes to AI providers; active-app-only and exclusion claims are vendor statements.

existingChecks.name: Microsoft Recall
existingChecks.observation: Publisher documentation describes opt-in local encrypted snapshots, semantic/visual recall, Windows Hello and Copilot+ hardware requirements. This is a Windows comparator, not a Mac runtime tested here.

existingChecks.name: ScreenMemory
existingChecks.observation: Standard $29 includes one year of updates, optional $5/year renewals; Lifetime $39. Free copy simultaneously lists 24-hour and unlimited history, so the inconsistency remains unresolved. Local OCR, timeline/calendar and application exclusions are advertised.

existingChecks.name: TimeScroll
existingChecks.observation: Site describes free native Swift/macOS14+, on-device MobileCLIP2 or local Ollama semantic search, AX/direct mode, thermal/duplicate backoff, local Whisper audio, MCP and an encrypted-vault beta. No power or privacy result independently measured.

existingChecks.name: Retrace (haseab)
existingChecks.observation: README identifies an early-development MIT project with periodic screenshots, Vision OCR, filtered search/timeline, analytics and resumable original-Rewind import. Repository claims, not executed acceptance.

existingChecks.name: Retrace (jhammant)
existingChecks.observation: README identifies Apache-2.0, macOS/Windows local capture and OS-native processing. It describes discarding raw frames after processing while retaining text, thumbnails and metadata. Cached documentation can lag current HEAD; no runtime or test claims independently reproduced.

existingChecks.name: rem
existingChecks.observation: README still describes an early local screen-memory project and asks for contributors. Repository labels MIT; no current packaged-app benchmark performed.

existingChecks.name: Unlost
existingChecks.observation: README labels Apache-2.0 and describes semantic/natural-language app/date search, screenshot text cropping and meeting transcripts. It marks local/provider LLM/agent and remote-storage integrations as future work; do not treat the roadmap as shipped.

existingChecks.name: Pensieve (formerly Memos)
existingChecks.observation: README describes local full-text/vector retrieval, chronological entity context, browser metadata, Ollama/OpenAI-compatible processing and plugins. It now advertises a v0.33 agent skill. Installing or benchmarking the current release was not part of this check.

existingChecks.name: Minne
existingChecks.observation: Site describes AX-based personal context, contextual drafting, a user-owned wiki, local MCP, optional local Ollama and external inference choices. It labels MIT and free. No local execution or inference-egress audit performed.

existingChecks.name: Omi
existingChecks.observation: Wearable homepage advertises a free plan and unlimited on-phone transcription. This does not verify current desktop-plan allowances; do not substitute wearable marketing for desktop pricing or behavior.

existingChecks.name: Granola
existingChecks.observation: Page displays Basic $0 with limited history, Business $14 and Enterprise $35/user/month. Business adds unlimited history, integrations, MCP/API; Enterprise adds policy/SSO/admin controls. No billing or runtime acceptance performed.

additionalComparators.name: OpenRecall
additionalComparators.plan: Open-source project; no subscription price established by these sources
additionalComparators.features: Periodic screenshots, local OCR, semantic history search and browser-based recall UI.
additionalComparators.difference: A direct screenshot-memory comparator missing from the 16-offering matrix.
additionalComparators.limits: No installation, code reuse or runtime benchmark. Review pinned version, license and model setup before a comparison.

additionalComparators.name: OpenHistory
additionalComparators.plan: Source/download available; paid plan not established by reviewed sources
additionalComparators.platform: macOS14+; Apple on-device summaries require compatible Apple Intelligence/macOS26+
additionalComparators.features: Permitted foreground AX context, no screenshots/audio/key logging; timeline, hourly/day summaries, optional inference providers and authenticated read-only local MCP.
additionalComparators.difference: A text-only, low-capture-surface comparator relevant to light mode and explicit cloud consent.
additionalComparators.limits: README contains both source-install and download language. Distribution, energy, privacy and runtime claims remain untested.

additionalComparators.name: silverfish
additionalComparators.features: AX text/metadata to SQLite FTS5; local Ollama, hardware/model-slot onboarding, hierarchical summaries, graph/wiki/profile, chat/drafting and MCP.
additionalComparators.difference: Useful reference for model-role setup and text-only local operation; no traction/rank inference from repository existence.
additionalComparators.limits: Cached README inspected, not code/runtime. Existing-database import and loopback-only inference are project claims, not verified interoperability/security results.

additionalComparators.name: Goldfish (goldfish.sh)
additionalComparators.licenseClaim: No open-source license established from reviewed primary pages
additionalComparators.plan: Free during beta; post-beta price not published on reviewed homepage
additionalComparators.features: AX text capture, on-device SQLite memory, contextual replies/chat and AI-tool integrations. Policy describes Cloudflare/Azure AI processing for user requests and background organization, plus dictation.
additionalComparators.difference: Local storage is distinct from local inference. Pattern masking explicitly preserves names, emails, phones, addresses and dates of birth for context.
additionalComparators.limits: Vendor policy claims, not independently audited. Not the unrelated coding-memory plugins or forensic tools named Goldfish.

remaining: Reverify unavailable pricing/service pages; distinguish cached source evidence from live HEAD.
Pin permissible versions and agree a reproducible owned workload before actual competitor benchmarks.
Do not infer privacy, energy, latency or accuracy from vendor documentation.
integration: Four additional profiles integrated; source-check labels, unavailable pricing and standalone text-capture requirement remain explicit. The historical initial queue/evidence is preserved in earlier commits.
